mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 1% coincident with a fall in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -1% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP is contracting but consumer confidence is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals supply-side disruptions in a tight labor market, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered instances, or the mechanism fails when commodity price shocks are the primary driver.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the real savings rate (proxied by RSAFS/GDPC1) above its long-run average for six months signals increased household saving and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 > long-run mean for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid credit expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than 12 months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL < 3% for 12 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or inflation exceeds 4% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of wage stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts related industries and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising mortgage rates.
